image_description: A close-up portrait of a Great White Pelican (or similar species) in profile, facing left. The bird features a long, pale pinkish-orange bill with a visible gular pouch, a distinct crest of feathers on the back of its head, and white/grey plumage. A second pelican is visible in the blurred background to the right. The setting appears to be aquatic with dark rocks or pilings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bill with distensible gular pouch extending from lower mandible.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the characteristic massive bill structure with the lower mandible forming the base of the gular pouch. The anatomy is consistent with a pelican.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bill is enormous and elongated, vastly exceeding head length, with bright orange, yellow, or pink coloration during breeding.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is significantly longer than the head. The coloration is a pale pink/orange hue, consistent with breeding or adult plumage for many pelican species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is large with prominent pouch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head proportions are correct for the species, and the pouch area is well-defined.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plumage is predominantly white, grey, or brown depending on species and season.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible plumage is white/light grey, which matches the description for Great White Pelicans or Australian Pelicans.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits heavy barrel-shaped torso of very large proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop focusing on the head and neck; the torso is largely out of frame or obscured by the angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings are extremely broad and long with dark flight feathers contrasting lighter body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wings are not visible in this head-and-neck portrait shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and webbed with all four toes connected.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely outside the frame.
The neck is visible, showing a graceful curve typical of waterbirds, though the full 'S' shape is partially constrained by the framing.
The tail is not visible in the frame.

artifact_observations.location: Feather edges on the head crest and neck
artifact_observations.reasoning: The fine feathers on the crest and along the neck edge have a slightly 'clumped' or overly smooth texture compared to the crispness expected in high-resolution wildlife photography. There is minor edge bleeding into the background bokeh.

The very tip of the upper bill appears slightly rounded and lacks the sharp, defined hook or nail typically seen on pelican bills. It blends slightly into the background rather than having a hard silhouette.
The eye appears somewhat flat and lacks the distinct catchlight reflection usually present in outdoor shots, giving it a slightly 'dead' or painted look.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and ensure the generated features (bill shape, crest) align with a real biological taxonomy rather than a generic 'bird' hallucination.
To rigorously check the boundary between the fine feather details and the background, identifying any melting or fusion artifacts that the human eye might miss due to depth-of-field blur.
To assess the overall photorealism, lighting consistency, and texture quality of the feathers and bill surface.

focus_areas: Bill tip definition and structural integrity
Feather texture realism vs. AI smoothing/clumping
Edge sharpness between subject and background (bokeh interaction)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the tip of the upper mandible; AI models often struggle with the precise hook geometry of pelican bills, resulting in rounding or melting. Also, scrutinize the 'crest' feathers on the back of the head—ensure they are individual strands and not a fused mass. Verify if the eye has a realistic catchlight appropriate for the lighting direction implied by the shadows on the bill.
